---
title: "How do I test whether a sample mean differs from a stated reference value?"
---

## Question

How do I test whether a sample mean differs from a stated reference value?

## Decide which method fits

Identify the null reference and whether the hypothesis is two-sided; inspect sample variation and design; run the one-sample t test with explicit confidence level.

## Worked example: PlantGrowth

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("PlantGrowth")
control <- subset(d, group=="ctrl")
fit <- ru_apply("one_sample_t", control, x="weight",
                reference=5, confidence=.95)
stopifnot(is.finite(fit$p.value))
```

This illustrative test compares the control group's mean to the stipulated value 5. It does not claim that 5 was the dataset's published null hypothesis. The p-value is not the probability the null hypothesis is true.

## Apply to another dataset

```r
ru_apply("one_sample_t", your_data, x="numeric_column", reference=your_null, confidence=.95)
```

If there is no meaningful reference mean, a one-sample test cannot answer the question. Report a mean and uncertainty instead.

Review assumptions and available input conditions with `ru_plan("one_sample_t")`. A valid computation does not itself verify the underlying study design.
